title: Definitions Summary
text: English Summary · Full Korean appendix · Korean Report Manuscript (PDF)

title: Definitions Summary
text:
Observed DOI-linked scope
The report analyzes policy-document references that can be linked to scholarly works through DOIs. This observed linkage excludes references that are not DOI-linked.

title: Definitions Summary
text:
Repeated-citation share
Repeated-citation share measures the share of distinct scholarly works cited by more than one policy document. In the baseline data, 48.1% of unique cited works are cited by at least two policy documents.
This value applies only to the observed DOI-linked citation scope.

title: Definitions Summary
text:
Domestic-citation share
Domestic-citation share is a country-level same-country citation measure. For a policy source country, it asks what share of citations point to research whose first-author country is the same country. First-author country means the country of the first author’s affiliated institution, not the author’s nationality.
The country assignment first uses the standardized first-author country mode. If that is unavailable, it uses a single unambiguous two-letter raw country code. Records with no code or conflicting codes remain unassigned. This metric uses only citations assigned a first-author country under that sequential rule. It is therefore better used as a diagnostic than as a simple country ranking.

title: Definitions Summary
text:
Domain-adjusted domestic-citation reference share
The domain-adjusted reference share combines the domain mix of cited research with each country’s first-author article share in the DOI-linked article sample. Each article is counted at most once per domain. This reference describes the linked sample and is not a measure of total global research production in OpenAlex.

title: Definitions Summary
text:
Country-assignment denominator
For Korean policy documents, 23,943 of 32,935 DOI-linked citations are assigned a research country; 8,992 (27.3%) remain unassigned and are reported separately. Country-level interpretation should therefore use the assigned-country denominator stated with each metric.

title: Methods Summary
text: English Summary · Full Korean methods page · Korean Report Manuscript (PDF)

title: Methods Summary
text:
Analysis scope

Data sources: Overton policy-document references and OpenAlex scholarly-work metadata.
Main citation unit: DOI-linked policy-document -> scholarly-work citation records.
Document unit: Overton policy documents deduplicated at the policy-document level.
Country comparisons assign the country of the first author’s affiliated institution, not the author’s nationality. The assignment uses the standardized country mode first, then a single unambiguous two-letter raw country code when the standardized value is unavailable.

title: Methods Summary
text:
Interpretation boundaries

The analysis covers observed DOI-linked policy-to-research citations, not the full policy universe.
Non-DOI evidence such as reports, legislation, web pages, and narrative references is outside the default indicators.
Hierarchical policy-source labels are collapsed to their top-level country, IGO, or EU category. The policy-source country is the country assigned to the organization that published the policy document. The IGO and EU categories are not countries, but they are compared at the same top level as source countries. Policy-source type labels can still overlap, so type totals are not mutually exclusive.
Records with no raw country code or conflicting raw codes remain unassigned and are reported separately. For Korean policy documents, 23,943 of 32,935 DOI-linked citations are assigned a research country; 8,992 (27.3%) remain unassigned.

title: Methods Summary
text:
Indicator definitions







Metric
Summary definition




Citation count
Number of DOI-linked policy-to-research citation records.


Unique works
Distinct OpenAlex works cited by policy documents.


Average citations per policy document
DOI-linked citations divided by policy documents with at least one DOI-linked citation in the policy-source or source-type group.


Repeat-citation share
Share of unique cited works cited by at least two policy documents.


Policy citations per paper
Policy citations divided by unique cited papers within a topic.


Share of unique papers published in 2022-2024
Share of unique cited papers published in 2022-2024 among papers with a known publication year through 2024 within a topic.


Domestic-citation share
Country-level same-country citation share, among citations assigned a first-author country under the sequential rule.

title: Methods Summary
text:
Denominator check
Do not compare indicator values until the denominator is clear. The most important denominator check is whether a metric uses all DOI-linked citation rows, unique works, policy documents, or only citations assigned a first-author country.

title: English Summary
text: Full Korean SI · Korean Report Manuscript (PDF)

title: English Summary
text:
Analysis summary
The report examines DOI-linked citations from policy documents in Overton to scholarly works in OpenAlex. It does not measure every policy document or every form of evidence. It summarizes the observable policy-to-research citation structure in the current linked data.
Prior studies show that policy citations do not simply reproduce scholarly citation rankings. Policy citations reach a selective subset of research, differ by field and document type, and can have a low article-level correlation with scholarly citations. The report uses this literature as an interpretive starting point; it does not directly compare scholarly and policy citation counts for Korean papers.
The report’s main finding is that the policy sources and fields in which Korean research is cited differ from the research countries and fields cited by Korean policy documents. The overall policy-source distribution provides context for this Korea-focused result rather than serving as a separate headline conclusion.

title: Public Reproducibility
Public Reproducibility
section: Additional inputs for a full rebuild
text:
Additional inputs for a full rebuild
A complete rebuild from source data requires licensed Overton policy-document and DOI-citation records, policy-source country and type metadata, and OpenAlex work, authorship, and topic data aligned to the report snapshot. The code archive’s Data_Insight/Report/Report_Runbook.md records the expected paths and build order. Credentials and local-only notebooks are not included.

title: Public Reproducibility
text:
Environment and version identification
The baseline environment uses Python 3.12, Quarto 1.4.550, Pandoc 3.1.3, and Google Chrome 150. Exact Python package versions are recorded in the environment list and manifest. The manuscript publication date is 2025-12-31, the aggregate run tag is 20251026, and the data snapshots are Overton 2025.02 and OpenAlex 2025.06.
